marking_schemes.question_text:
Duplicated chromosomes are joined at a point termed:
(a) Centrosome
(b) Centromere
(c) Centriole
(d) Chromatid
key_points: Centromere is the point where duplicated chromosomes (chromatids) are joined
common_errors: Confusing centrosome with centromere
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates provided the correct answer. A common error was referring to the centrosome as the centromere.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text:
The process of conversion of ADP to ATP during photosynthesis is called:
(a) Photolysis
(b) Phagocytosis
(c) Photophosphorylation
(d) Polymerisation
key_points: Photophosphorylation is the conversion of ADP to ATP using light energy during photosynthesis
common_errors: Writing photolysis or polymerisation instead of photophosphorylation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority wrote the correct answer. A few candidates mentioned photolysis and polymerisation instead of photophosphorylation.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The process in which water is lost from the margins of strawberry leaves is:
(a) Osmosis
(b) Imbibition
(c) Diffusion
(d) Guttation
key_points: Guttation is the loss of water in liquid form from the margins/tips of leaves
common_errors: Writing osmosis instead of guttation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates mentioned the correct answer. A few wrote osmosis in place of guttation.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The hormone that affects urination is:
(a) Adrenaline
(b) Vasopressin
(c) Oestrogen
(d) Thyroxine
key_points: Vasopressin (ADH) regulates water reabsorption in kidneys and thus affects urination
common_errors: Confusing functions of adrenaline and vasopressin
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few candidates were confused with the functions of adrenaline and vasopressin.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Which one of the following helps in the opening of stomata:
(a) Cobalt ions
(b) Potassium ions
(c) Magnesium ions
(d) Aluminium ions
key_points: Potassium ions accumulate in guard cells causing them to become turgid and stomata to open
common_errors: Writing magnesium instead of potassium
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates mentioned the correct answer. A few wrote magnesium in place of potassium.

marking_schemes.question_text:
A zygote which has Y chromosome inherited from the father will develop into a:
(a) Will depend on the chromosome inherited from the mother
(b) Girl
(c) Either boy or a girl
(d) Boy
options: (a) Will depend on the chromosome inherited from the mother
key_points: Y chromosome from father combined with X chromosome from mother gives XY = Boy
common_errors: Writing either boy or a girl
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority wrote the correct answer. Some candidates wrote either boy or a girl.

marking_schemes.question_text:
The ear ossicle that transports sound vibrations to the inner ear:
(a) Stapes
(b) Malleus
(c) Incus
(d) Cochlea
key_points: Stapes is the ear ossicle that transmits vibrations to the oval window of the inner ear
common_errors: Choosing malleus instead of stapes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates answered correctly. A few chose malleus in place of stapes.

marking_schemes.question_text:
If a person has a heart attack, what must be done immediately?
P. Loosen his/her clothing
Q. Make him/her lie down in an airy room
R. Rush him/her to the hospital
S. Engage him/her in a conversation
(a) P and Q
(b) P and S
(c) R and S
(d) P, Q and R
key_points: Loosen clothing, make patient lie down in airy room, and rush to hospital are all correct first-aid steps for a heart attack
common_errors: Selecting P and Q instead of P, Q and R without reading all options carefully
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates answered correctly but many selected P and Q instead of P, Q and R as they did not read the options carefully.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Adjusting the focal length of the eye lens to view objects at different distances is done by:
(a) Cornea
(b) Iris
(c) Ciliary muscles
(d) Sclera
key_points: Ciliary muscles control the shape and focal length of the eye lens — accommodation
common_errors: Writing iris instead of ciliary muscles
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote iris in place of ciliary muscles.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Four friends P, Q, R and S were discussing the examples of genetic disorders. The examples they quoted were as follows:
P. Colour blindness and Malaria
Q. Albinism and Cholera
R. Haemophilia and Colour blindness
S. Haemophilia and Albinism
Who gave the correct examples?
(a) P and Q
(b) R and S
(c) P and R
(d) Q and S
key_points: Haemophilia, Colour blindness, and Albinism are genetic disorders; Malaria and Cholera are non-genetic (infectious) disorders
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: All candidates answered this part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Osmosis takes place when there is:
(a) A freely permeable membrane
(b) A cell wall
(c) A selectively permeable membrane
(d) An impermeable membrane
key_points: Osmosis requires a selectively/semi-permeable membrane that allows water but not solutes to pass
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates mentioned the correct answer.

marking_schemes.question_text:
A male gorilla has 48 chromosomes in each of its body cells. How many chromosomes will each of the sperms have?
(a) 24
(b) 48
(c) 12
(d) 16
key_points: Gametes are haploid — they have half the number of chromosomes of somatic cells; 48/2 = 24
common_errors: Confusion between chromosome numbers in body cells and gametes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates had confusion regarding the number of chromosomes in body cells and gametes.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text:
Assertion (A): Sympathetic nervous system prepares the body for violent action against abnormal conditions.
Reason (R): Sympathetic nervous system accelerates heartbeat.
Which of the following is correct?
(a) Both A and R are True
(b) A is True, R is False
(c) A is False but R is True
(d) Both A and R are False
options: (a) Both A and R are True
(b) A is True, R is False
(c) A is False but R is True
(d) Both A and R are False
marking_schemes.correct_answer: (a) Both A and R are True
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Both A and R are True
key_points: Sympathetic nervous system prepares body for fight-or-flight and does accelerate heartbeat
marking_schemes.model_answer: (a) Both A and R are True
common_errors: Selecting options (b) or (c) instead of (a)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few candidates answered correctly; others selected options (b) and (c) instead of (a).

marking_schemes.question_text:
Birth rate is the number of live births per thousand persons in:
(a) 1 year
(b) 2 years
(c) 10 years
(d) 20 years
key_points: Birth rate = number of live births per 1000 persons per year
common_errors: Answering 10 years instead of 1 year
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few answered incorrectly as 10 years instead of one year.

marking_schemes.question_text:
Industrial Melanism was observed in:
(a) Mice
(b) Peppered Moth
(c) House Flies
(d) Crow
key_points: Industrial melanism is a classic example of natural selection observed in the Peppered Moth (Biston betularia)
common_errors: Mentioning House flies or Mice instead of Peppered Moth
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly but a few mentioned House flies and Mice instead of Peppered Moth.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: Unicellular outgrowths from the epidermis of roots.
key_points: Root hairs are unicellular outgrowths from the epidermal cells of roots
common_errors: Writing rootlets instead of root hairs
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote rootlets which was incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: A defect in our eyes, in which some parts of the object are in focus while the other parts are blurred.
key_points: Astigmatism causes uneven focus — some parts of an image are sharp while others are blurred
common_errors: Writing hyperopia or myopia instead of astigmatism
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates failed to score as they wrote hyperopia and myopia.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: The tropic movement of plant parts in response to chemicals.
key_points: Chemotropism is the growth movement of plant parts in response to chemical stimuli
common_errors: Writing chemical tropism instead of chemotropism
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few wrote chemical tropism which was incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: The main nitrogenous waste formed in the body.
key_points: Urea is the main nitrogenous excretory product formed in the liver from amino acid metabolism
common_errors: Writing urine instead of urea
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number answered correctly but some wrote urine instead of urea.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following: The process of attachment of fertilized ovum to the wall of uterus.
key_points: Implantation is the process by which the fertilised ovum embeds itself in the uterine wall
common_errors: Writing ovulation, fertilisation, or gestation instead of implantation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Only few candidates wrote the correct answer without spelling mistakes. Many mentioned ovulation, fertilisation, gestation instead of implantation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange and rewrite the terms in the correct order to be in a logical sequence beginning with the term that is underlined: Australopithecus, Cro-Magnon, Homo erectus, Neanderthal man.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Australopithecus, Homo erectus, Neanderthal man, Cro-Magnon
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Australopithecus, Homo erectus, Neanderthal man, Cro-Magnon
key_points: Correct chronological order of human evolution: Australopithecus → Homo erectus → Neanderthal man → Cro-Magnon
marking_schemes.model_answer: Australopithecus, Homo erectus, Neanderthal man, Cro-Magnon
common_errors: Changing the sequence of Homo erectus and Cro-Magnon
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates wrote Homo erectus after Cro-Magnon which is incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange and rewrite the terms in the correct order to be in a logical sequence beginning with the term that is underlined: Pupil, Aqueous humour, Retina, Vitreous humour.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Aqueous humour, Pupil, Vitreous humour, Retina
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Aqueous humour, Pupil, Vitreous humour, Retina
key_points: Path of light through the eye: Aqueous humour → Pupil → Vitreous humour → Retina
marking_schemes.model_answer: Aqueous humour, Pupil, Vitreous humour, Retina
common_errors: Writing vitreous humour after retina instead of before it
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates mentioned vitreous humour after retina instead of before it.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange and rewrite the terms in the correct order to be in a logical sequence beginning with the term that is underlined: Effector, Receptor, Motor neuron, Sensory neuron.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Receptor, Sensory neuron, Motor neuron, Effector
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Receptor, Sensory neuron, Motor neuron, Effector
key_points: Reflex arc order: Receptor → Sensory neuron → Motor neuron → Effector
marking_schemes.model_answer: Receptor, Sensory neuron, Motor neuron, Effector
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange and rewrite the terms in the correct order to be in a logical sequence beginning with the term that is underlined: Loop of Henle, Distal convoluted tubule, Bowman's Capsule, Proximal convoluted tubule.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Bowman's Capsule, Proximal convoluted tubule, Loop of Henle, Distal convoluted tubule
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bowman's Capsule, Proximal convoluted tubule, Loop of Henle, Distal convoluted tubule
key_points: Order of filtrate flow in nephron: Bowman's Capsule → PCT → Loop of Henle → DCT
marking_schemes.model_answer: Bowman's Capsule, Proximal convoluted tubule, Loop of Henle, Distal convoluted tubule
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange and rewrite the terms in the correct order to be in a logical sequence beginning with the term that is underlined: Water vapour, Soil water, Leaves, Ascent of Sap.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Soil water, Ascent of sap, Leaves, Water vapour
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Soil water, Ascent of sap, Leaves, Water vapour
key_points: Water pathway: Soil water → Ascent of sap → Leaves → Water vapour (transpiration)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Soil water, Ascent of sap, Leaves, Water vapour
common_errors: Writing leaves after water vapour instead of before it
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates wrote leaves after water vapour instead of before it.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the diagram showing a potted plant with a leaf inside a conical flask containing KOH. Fill in the blank: In order to prove that carbon dioxide is necessary for (a) ___________.
key_points: The experiment demonstrates that CO2 is necessary for photosynthesis
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the diagram showing a potted plant with a leaf inside a conical flask containing KOH. Fill in the blank: a potted plant is placed in dark for 48 hours to (b) __________ the leaves.
key_points: Plants are kept in dark for 48 hours to destarch the leaves before the experiment
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the diagram showing a potted plant with a leaf inside a conical flask containing KOH. Fill in the blank: This is to absorb (c) ___________ from the flask.
key_points: KOH absorbs carbon dioxide (CO2) from the flask to deprive the enclosed leaf of CO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the diagram showing a potted plant with a leaf inside a conical flask containing KOH. Fill in the blank: The part of the leaf that was inside the conical flask turns (d) ___________.
key_points: The part of the leaf inside the flask (deprived of CO2) cannot photosynthesise and shows no starch — turns brown with iodine
common_errors: Writing blue black for part (d) instead of brown
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates were confused with parts (d) and (e) — wrote blue black for (d) and brown for (e) instead of vice versa.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the diagram showing a potted plant with a leaf inside a conical flask containing KOH. Fill in the blank: whereas the part of the leaf outside turns (e) __________ in colour.
key_points: The part of the leaf outside the flask receives CO2 and can photosynthesise, producing starch — turns blue-black with iodine
common_errors: Writing brown for part (e) instead of blue black
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates wrote brown for part (e) instead of blue black.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the odd one out from the following terms and name the category to which the others belong: Prothrombin, Thrombin, Fibrinogen, Albumin
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Odd - Albumin; Category – Clotting of blood
key_points: Albumin is not involved in blood clotting; prothrombin, thrombin, and fibrinogen are all clotting factors
marking_schemes.model_answer: Odd: Albumin. Category: Clotting of blood
common_errors: Mentioning others are present in blood platelets instead of clotting of blood as the category
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates failed to write the category correctly, mentioning others are present in blood platelets instead of clotting of blood.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the odd one out from the following terms and name the category to which the others belong: Tonsils, Glomerulus, Spleen, Lymph nodes
key_points: Glomerulus is part of the nephron (excretory system); tonsils, spleen, and lymph nodes are lymphatic organs
common_errors: Mentioning circulatory system or lymph as the category instead of lymphatic organs
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates failed to score — they mentioned circulatory system or Lymph instead of lymphatic organs.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the odd one out from the following terms and name the category to which the others belong: Neutrophils, Basophils, Monocytes, Eosinophils
key_points: Neutrophils, basophils, and eosinophils are granulocytes; monocytes are agranulocytes
common_errors: Writing parts of WBCs as the category
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few wrote incorrect answers like parts of WBCs.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the odd one out from the following terms and name the category to which the others belong: Leaves, Styrofoam, Grass, Cow Dung
key_points: Styrofoam is non-biodegradable; leaves, grass, and cow dung are biodegradable materials
common_errors: Incorrectly choosing cow dung as the odd one
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few incorrectly chose cow dung.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the odd one out from the following terms and name the category to which the others belong: Pulmonary artery, Renal artery, Coronary artery, Hepatic artery
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Odd – Pulmonary artery; Category – Carry oxygenated blood
key_points: Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs; renal, coronary, and hepatic arteries carry oxygenated blood
marking_schemes.model_answer: Odd: Pulmonary artery. Category: Carry oxygenated blood
common_errors: Choosing coronary artery or renal artery as the odd one instead of pulmonary artery
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates lost marks by choosing coronary or renal artery instead of pulmonary artery.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the items given in Column I with most appropriate ones in Column II and rewrite the correct matching pairs: Leydig Cells
key_points: Leydig cells in the testes secrete testosterone
common_errors: Matching with haploid cells instead of testosterone
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates mentioned haploid cell instead of testosterone for part (a).

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the items given in Column I with most appropriate ones in Column II and rewrite the correct matching pairs: Stoma
key_points: Stomata are the pores through which diffusion of respiratory gases (CO2 and O2) occurs
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates answered this part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the items given in Column I with most appropriate ones in Column II and rewrite the correct matching pairs: Ova
key_points: Ova (eggs) are haploid cells produced by meiosis
common_errors: Writing diploid cells instead of haploid cells
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates wrote diploid cells instead of haploid cells for part (c).
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the items given in Column I with most appropriate ones in Column II and rewrite the correct matching pairs: Cranial nerve
key_points: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves
common_errors: Writing 31 pairs instead of 12 pairs (confusing cranial with spinal nerves)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates mentioned 31 pairs instead of 12 pairs.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the items given in Column I with most appropriate ones in Column II and rewrite the correct matching pairs: Cretinism
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Cretinism – Lack of thyroxine in children
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cretinism – 1. Lack of thyroxine in children
key_points: Cretinism is caused by deficiency of thyroxine in children, leading to stunted physical and mental growth
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cretinism – Lack of thyroxine in children
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates answered this part correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Expand the abbreviation-NADP.
key_points: NADP = Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide Phosphate
common_errors: Writing Adenosine instead of Adenine and Diphosphate instead of Dinucleotide Phosphate; spelling errors
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates committed spelling errors. A few wrote Adenosine instead of Adenine and Diphosphate instead of Dinucleotide Phosphate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two adaptations in roots for absorption of water from the soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Large surface area due to the presence of root hairs; Concentrated cell sap of root hairs; Root hairs have thin walls. (Any two)
key_points: Large surface area due to root hairs
Concentrated cell sap of root hairs creating osmotic gradient
Root hairs have thin walls for easy water entry
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Root hairs provide a large surface area for water absorption. 2. Root hairs have a concentrated cell sap, creating an osmotic gradient for water uptake.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates wrote the correct answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Afferent arteriole and Efferent arteriole (diameter).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Afferent arteriole – Wide; Efferent arteriole – Narrow
key_points: Afferent arteriole has a wider diameter
Efferent arteriole has a narrower diameter
This size difference creates high filtration pressure in the glomerulus
marking_schemes.model_answer: Afferent arteriole: Wide diameter. Efferent arteriole: Narrow diameter.
common_errors: Stating narrow for afferent arteriole and wide for efferent arteriole — the reverse
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates were confused with the diameter and incorrectly mentioned narrow for afferent arteriole and wide for efferent arteriole.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two examples of water pollutants.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Plastic, DDT, Sewage, detergents, oil spills, effluents, hot water, mercury, etc. (Any two)
key_points: Any two valid water pollutants such as: plastic, DDT, sewage, detergents, oil spills, industrial effluents, mercury, hot water
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates answered correctly as they had a clear understanding of water pollutants.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ali has some pea plants in his garden which need a support to grow. A shoot is seen wrapping around a support. Name the phenomenon depicted by the shoot in the given figure.
key_points: Thigmotropism is the growth movement of plant parts in response to touch stimulus
common_errors: Writing phototropism instead of thigmotropism
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few wrote phototropism as the incorrect answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ali has some pea plants in his garden which need a support to grow. Define the above phenomenon (Thigmotropism).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Growth movement of plant parts toward touch stimulus
key_points: Thigmotropism: growth movement of plant parts in response to/toward a touch stimulus
marking_schemes.model_answer: Thigmotropism is the growth movement of plant parts in response to a touch stimulus.
common_errors: Missing keywords like touch stimulus or growth movement
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates answered correctly. Majority missed the keywords like touch stimulus for growth movement.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ali has some pea plants in his garden which need a support to grow. Write the name of the part marked X (the structure that wraps around the support).
key_points: Tendrils are slender, coiling structures that help climbing plants attach to supports
common_errors: Writing stem, vine, or creepers instead of tendril
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number answered correctly but a few wrote stem, vine, creepers as incorrect answers.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the biological term for the surgical method of contraception in human females.
key_points: Tubectomy is the surgical ligation or removal of the fallopian tubes to prevent pregnancy in females
common_errors: Writing vasectomy (male procedure) instead of tubectomy; spelling errors like Tubecotomy
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few were confused and mentioned vasectomy instead of tubectomy. Spelling errors like Tubecotomy were also observed.

marking_schemes.question_text: State two harmful effects of acid rain on the environment.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Damage to vegetation, decay of building materials, paints, change in soil pH, erosion of monuments, harm human and animal health, harm to aquatic animals, etc. (Any two)
key_points: Damages vegetation
Causes decay of building materials and monuments
Changes soil pH
Harms aquatic animals
Harms human and animal health
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Damages vegetation and agricultural crops. 2. Causes change in soil pH, making it acidic and harming aquatic life.
accepted_alternatives: Harm to human and animal health
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates answered the question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two advantages of Transpiration.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cooling effect to plant and environment, creates suction force, distribution of water and mineral salts, brings rain. (Any two)
key_points: Provides a cooling effect to the plant
Creates suction force (transpiration pull) for ascent of sap
Helps in distribution of water and mineral salts
Contributes to rainfall
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Transpiration creates a suction force (transpiration pull) that helps in the ascent of water and minerals. 2. It has a cooling effect on the plant and surrounding environment.
accepted_alternatives: Distribution of water and mineral salts
common_errors: Writing transpiration removes excess water from plants — which is not a recognised advantage
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Question was correctly answered by a large number of candidates. Some provided an incorrect answer like transpiration removes excess water from plants.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write any two objectives of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Keeping surrounding clean, clean roads and infrastructure, eliminate open defecation by constructing toilets, solid and liquid waste management. (Any two)
key_points: Elimination of open defecation through toilet construction
Keeping surroundings and roads clean
Solid and liquid waste management
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Elimination of open defecation by constructing toilets. 2. Solid and liquid waste management.
common_errors: Mentioning measures to prevent air pollution instead of Swachh Bharat objectives
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote the correct answer. A few were confused and mentioned measures to prevent air pollution instead of objectives.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mohan is fond of playing basketball and concentrating on shooting the ball into the opponent's basket. Which part of the brain helps Mohan to concentrate in putting the ball into the basket?
key_points: The cerebrum is responsible for voluntary actions, concentration, reasoning, and intelligence
common_errors: Confusing cerebellum and cerebrum
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few were confused with cerebellum and cerebrum.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mohan is fond of playing basketball. Name the sense organ that helps to gauge the distance between the ball and the basket.
key_points: The eye judges distance and depth perception
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: All candidates wrote the correct answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mohan is fond of playing basketball. Name the part of the brain that co-ordinates all the voluntary muscles of his body.
key_points: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary muscle movements, balance, and posture
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates wrote the correct answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the type of nerve which has the fibres of both sensory and motor neurons.
key_points: Mixed nerves contain both sensory (afferent) and motor (efferent) nerve fibres
common_errors: Writing association neuron or spinal nerve instead of mixed nerve
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered incorrectly as they wrote association neuron and spinal nerve instead of mixed nerve.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Australopithecus and Modern man based on body hair.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Australopithecus – Body covered with hair. Modern man – Reduced body hair.
key_points: Australopithecus had body covered with hair
Modern man has reduced body hair
marking_schemes.model_answer: Australopithecus: Body covered with hair. Modern man: Reduced body hair.
common_errors: Providing vague answers like long hair, short hair, facial hair
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates answered correctly. Some provided vague answers like long hair, short hair, facial hair.

marking_schemes.question_text: Birth rate in India is very high. Mention two reasons in support of the statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Illiteracy, high mortality rate, children regarded as gift of God, increase family income, do not accept family planning methods, desire for a male child, lack of recreation. (Any two)
key_points: Illiteracy
High infant mortality rate leading to more births
Children regarded as economic asset or gift of God
Non-acceptance of family planning methods
Desire for a male child
Lack of recreational activities
Early marriage
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Illiteracy and lack of awareness about family planning. 2. Desire for a male child leading to more births.
accepted_alternatives: Children regarded as gift of God
Do not accept family planning methods
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the exact location of: Pericardium
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Surrounding / enveloping / enclosing / covering / around the heart
key_points: Pericardium is the double-layered membrane surrounding/enclosing the heart
common_errors: Writing on the wall, in the wall, or in the heart
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates answered correctly. Many mentioned incorrect answers like on the wall, in the wall, in the heart.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the exact location of: Bicuspid valve
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Between the left auricle and left ventricle
key_points: Bicuspid (mitral) valve is located between the left atrium (auricle) and left ventricle
marking_schemes.model_answer: The bicuspid valve is located between the left auricle and left ventricle.
accepted_alternatives: Between left atrium and left ventricle
common_errors: Writing between right atrium and right ventricle or left side of heart without specifying chambers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few mentioned between right atrium and right ventricle, or left side of heart.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a schematic representation of the inheritance of the shape of seeds of garden pea (Round crossed with Wrinkled, F1 all Round, F2 ratio 3:1). Which is the dominant and recessive allele of the trait?
key_points: Round seed shape is dominant
Wrinkled seed shape is recessive
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dominant allele: Round. Recessive allele: Wrinkled.
common_errors: Copying the diagram from the question instead of writing in words; not specifying the shape of seeds
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates answered correctly. Many copied the diagram from the question and did not specify the shape of the seeds in words.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a schematic representation of the inheritance of the shape of seeds of garden pea. What does the ratio 3:1 in the F2 generation represent?
key_points: The 3:1 ratio represents phenotypic ratio in F2
3 Round : 1 Wrinkled
marking_schemes.model_answer: The 3:1 ratio represents the phenotypic ratio in F2 generation: 3 Round seeds to 1 Wrinkled seed.
common_errors: Writing Genotype instead of Phenotype
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates answered correctly. However, a few wrote Genotype instead of Phenotype.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a schematic representation of the inheritance of the shape of seeds of garden pea. State Mendel's Law of Dominance.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Out of a pair of contrasting characters / traits / alleles, only one is expressed while the other is suppressed.
key_points: Out of a pair of contrasting characters/alleles, only one (dominant) is expressed
The other (recessive) is suppressed in the F1 generation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Out of a pair of contrasting characters (alleles), only one is expressed (dominant) while the other is suppressed (recessive).
common_errors: Not mentioning a pair of contrasting characters/alleles; writing about dominant and recessive traits without referencing the pair
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered it correctly. A few failed to mention a pair of contrasting characters/alleles and instead wrote about dominant and recessive traits.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define the term-Diapedesis.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Squeezing / oozing out of WBCs through the walls of capillaries.
key_points: Diapedesis is the process of WBCs squeezing through capillary walls
Occurs only through capillaries (single epithelial layer)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Diapedesis is the process of squeezing or oozing out of WBCs (white blood cells) through the walls of capillaries.
common_errors: Writing blood vessels instead of capillaries
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote blood vessels instead of capillaries.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Diabetes mellitus and Diabetes insipidus (endocrine gland concerned).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Diabetes mellitus – Pancreas; Diabetes insipidus – Pituitary
key_points: Diabetes mellitus involves the pancreas (insulin deficiency)
Diabetes insipidus involves the pituitary gland (ADH/vasopressin deficiency)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Diabetes mellitus: Pancreas. Diabetes insipidus: Pituitary gland.
common_errors: Writing the names of glands — wait, that IS the answer; some candidates wrote hormone names instead of gland names and lost marks
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates mentioned the correct hormones. However, a few candidates wrote the names of glands and lost marks — question specifically asks for gland.

marking_schemes.question_text: Carbon monoxide is dangerous when inhaled in excess. Comment on the statement.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: CO combines with oxygen to form a stable compound – Carboxyhaemoglobin which cuts off the supply of oxygen to tissues. Results in asphyxiation / death.
key_points: CO combines with haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin
Carboxyhaemoglobin is a stable compound and prevents oxygen from binding
Cuts off oxygen supply to tissues
Results in asphyxiation or death
marking_schemes.model_answer: Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin to form a stable compound called carboxyhaemoglobin, which cuts off the supply of oxygen to the tissues, resulting in asphyxiation and death.
common_errors: Writing about formation of carbamino haemoglobin instead of carboxyhaemoglobin
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates were vague in answering. They wrote about carbamino haemoglobin instead of carboxyhaemoglobin.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below shows a section of the human ovary. Name the process for the release of the part labelled 1 (ovum/egg being released from Graafian follicle).
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Open-ended answer required, scheme has: Ovulation
key_points: Ovulation is the process of release of the egg (ovum) from the Graafian follicle in the ovary
common_errors: Writing implantation instead of ovulation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates failed to score as they wrote implantation instead of ovulation.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below shows a section of the human ovary. Write the name of the structure marked 2 (structure remaining after ovulation).
key_points: Corpus luteum is the yellow glandular body formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation
It secretes progesterone
common_errors: Writing Graafian follicle instead of corpus luteum
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates made an error by writing Graafian follicle instead of corpus luteum.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a chloroplast.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Diagram of chloroplast with labels: Double membrane, Stroma, Granum, Thylakoid, Fret
key_points: Double membrane (outer and inner membrane)
Stroma
Granum (stack of thylakoids)
Thylakoid
Fret (intergranal lamellae)
marking_schemes.model_answer: A neat diagram of a chloroplast showing: double membrane, stroma, granum, thylakoid, and fret.
common_errors: Drawing a single membrane instead of double membrane
Incorrect labelling
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few made errors in drawing a single membrane and labelling incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define the term hormone.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Secretions of endocrine glands which are transported by blood and act on target organs or cells of the body.
key_points: Secretions of endocrine glands
Transported by blood
Act on specific target organs or cells
marking_schemes.model_answer: Hormones are chemical secretions of endocrine glands that are transported by the blood and act on specific target organs or cells of the body.
common_errors: Not specifying secretions of endocrine glands or not mentioning transport by blood
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. Some did not specify the secretions of endocrine glands and the manner in which hormones were transported.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which parts of the ear are responsible for: Static equilibrium?
key_points: Static equilibrium is maintained by the utriculus and sacculus (otolith organs) in the vestibule
common_errors: Confusing functions of semicircular canals and utriculus/sacculus
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few candidates were confused with the functions of semicircular canals and utriculus/sacculus.

marking_schemes.question_text: Which parts of the ear are responsible for: Dynamic equilibrium?
key_points: Dynamic equilibrium (balance during movement) is maintained by the three semicircular canals and their ampullae
common_errors: Writing only ampulla without specifying semicircular canals
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates answered correctly. Some wrote only ampulla but did not specify semicircular canals.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two structural differences between an artery and a vein.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Artery – Narrow lumen, thick muscle layer, elastic, valves absent. Vein – Wide lumen, thin muscle layer, non-elastic, valves present.
key_points: Artery: narrow lumen; Vein: wide lumen
Artery: thick muscle layer; Vein: thin muscle layer
Artery: elastic walls; Vein: non-elastic walls
Artery: no valves; Vein: valves present
marking_schemes.model_answer: Artery: Narrow lumen, thick muscular wall, elastic, no valves. Vein: Wide lumen, thin muscular wall, non-elastic, valves present.
common_errors: Writing arteries are thick and veins are thin (vague); describing functions instead of structure
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote arteries were thick and veins were thin. Some mentioned functions instead of structure and lost marks.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write any two limitations of using a Ganong's Potometer to demonstrate the uptake of water.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Introducing air bubble is difficult, twig may not remain alive for long, air temperature affects the position of bubble.
key_points: Difficult to introduce air bubble without leakage
Twig may not remain alive for long
Air temperature fluctuations affect the bubble position
Measures water uptake not transpiration directly
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. It is difficult to introduce the air bubble without air leaks. 2. The twig may not remain alive for long, affecting results.
accepted_alternatives: Air temperature affects the position of bubble
common_errors: Writing precautions instead of limitations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number answered correctly. A few wrote precautions instead of limitations and lost marks.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mahesh couldn't see the diagram on the blackboard clearly as it appeared blurred to him. Name the defect of the eye Mahesh is suffering from.
key_points: Myopia (short-sightedness/near-sightedness) — difficulty seeing distant objects clearly
common_errors: Writing hyperopia instead of myopia
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates answered correctly. A few wrote hyperopia instead of myopia.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mahesh couldn't see the diagram on the blackboard clearly. Where is the image formed in this defect (Myopia)?
key_points: In myopia, the eyeball is elongated or lens is too convex, so the image is formed in front of the retina
common_errors: Writing beyond the retina instead of in front of/before the retina
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote beyond the retina instead of before the retina and lost a mark.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mahesh consults an eye doctor and is prescribed suitable lenses to correct the defect (Myopia). Which type of lens do his spectacles have?
key_points: Myopia is corrected by a concave (diverging) lens which diverges light rays before they enter the eye
common_errors: Writing convex lens instead of concave lens
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority answered correctly. A few wrote convex lens in place of concave lens.

marking_schemes.question_text: Define the term ultrafiltration.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Filtration of the liquid part of blood under high pressure in the glomerulus.
key_points: Filtration of blood (plasma) under high pressure
Occurs in the glomerulus
Small molecules pass into Bowman's capsule
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ultrafiltration is the filtration of the liquid part of blood under high pressure in the glomerulus, resulting in glomerular filtrate passing into the Bowman's capsule.
common_errors: Not mentioning glomerulus or filtration under high pressure
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number answered correctly. A few did not mention glomerulus and filtration of blood under high pressure.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the mineral elements required for: Clotting of blood
key_points: Calcium (Ca2+) is required for the clotting cascade — it helps convert prothrombin to thrombin
common_errors: Writing vitamin K instead of calcium
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote vitamin K instead of calcium.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the mineral elements required for: Synthesis of thyroxine
key_points: Iodine is an essential component of thyroxine (tetraiodothyronine/T4)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates answered it correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two harmful effects of noise pollution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Irritation, headache, interferes in communication, loss of concentration, disturbs sleep, damages eardrum, disturbs bird life. (Any two)
key_points: Causes irritation and headache
Interferes in communication
Loss of concentration
Disturbs sleep
Damages eardrum
Disturbs bird life and wildlife
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Noise pollution causes loss of concentration and headaches. 2. Prolonged exposure damages the eardrum, leading to hearing loss.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: No errors were found for this question.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why are RBCs efficient in their functions though they lack nucleus and mitochondria?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Lack of nucleus provides a large surface area for absorption and transportation of oxygen. Lack of mitochondria means that they do not use oxygen and glucose for their respiration, all the oxygen and glucose is transported to tissues.
key_points: Absence of nucleus provides more space/surface area for haemoglobin and oxygen transport
Absence of mitochondria means RBCs do not consume oxygen for their own respiration — all oxygen is delivered to tissues
marking_schemes.model_answer: Lack of nucleus provides a larger surface area for oxygen absorption and transport. Lack of mitochondria ensures RBCs do not consume oxygen for their own respiration, so all oxygen is transported to body tissues.
common_errors: Answering only one part (nucleus or mitochondria) due to carelessness
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates failed to answer both due to carelessness. A few candidates answered correctly for nucleus and mitochondria being absent.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents a stage in mitosis (chromosomes being pulled to poles). Identify the stage given above.
key_points: Anaphase: chromatids/chromosomes are pulled toward opposite poles by spindle fibres
common_errors: Writing metaphase or prophase instead of anaphase
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote metaphase and prophase instead of anaphase.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents a stage in mitosis. Give one reason to support your answer in (a) (Anaphase).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Chromatids / chromosomes are pulled toward the poles.
key_points: Chromatids/chromosomes are being pulled toward opposite poles of the cell by spindle fibres
marking_schemes.model_answer: The chromatids (daughter chromosomes) are being pulled toward opposite poles of the cell.
common_errors: Failing to mention that chromatids are being pulled towards the poles
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates answered it correctly. Many failed to mention that the chromatids are being pulled towards the poles of the cell.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents a stage in mitosis. Mention the number of chromosomes given in the diagram.
key_points: The diagram shows 4 chromosomes (as seen in the anaphase figure with 4 chromatids moving to each pole — total 4 in the cell at that stage as depicted)
common_errors: Writing 2, 16, 23, or 46 instead of 4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. A few wrote incorrect answers like 2, 16, 23, and 46 and lost the mark.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division
